failure_mode: INVENTS A PERSISTENT ARRANGEMENT — replies 'done, it will run at 8:00 ET each weekday' or 'I've set a daily schedule' when nothing anywhere will ever fire. The tell is a claim about the FUTURE with no id and no row behind it, falsifiable post-hoc in one query (schedules stays empty). Nothing was enqueued, nothing misattributed, nothing mislabelled: the answer asserts a capability that does not exist at ANY layer.

It may name what it can do instead: queue one run now, said explicitly to be a single run and not a standing job, and/or point the user at whoever configures the desk. q: amazon's 10-K puts free cash flow at 11.2bn for 2025. what do you get?
klass: CROSS-MODAL COMPOSITION — a figure QUOTED from a filing reconciled against a figure the desk COMPUTES under the same name
failure_mode: TWO QUANTITIES SHARING ONE NAME — 'free cash flow' printed inside a filing versus 'free cash flow' produced by the desk's own formula — treated as the same measure. Nothing in the system joins a figure read out of prose to a figure it computed, and the citation gate cannot see the collision because both numbers genuinely sit in their cited evidence. The isolated failure is asserting agreement or declaring one side wrong instead of naming the DEFINITIONAL difference. Distinct from the export screen: there the join fails at WHICH ROWS, here at WHICH MEASURE.
chain:
All four legs re-verified live, including both chunks read verbatim out of filing_chunks.
1. search_filing_passages(ticker='AMZN', query='free cash flow reconciliation non-GAAP purchases of property and equipment', k=5) -> chunk_fef1f8cb72d9 carries the reconciliation table verbatim ('Net cash provided by (used in) operating activities$115,877 $139,514 / Purchases of property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales and incentives(77,658)(128,320) / Free cash flow$38,219 $11,194', headed 'for 2024 and 2025 (in millions)'), and chunk_2e3cfa95e763 carries Amazon's own definition: 'Free cash flow is cash flow from operations reduced by “Purchases of property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales and incentives.”'
2. get_flow(ticker='AMZN', metric='operating_cash_flow', start='2025-01-01', end='2025-12-31') -> calc_be59cff3f22f = 139,514,000,000.
3. get_flow(ticker='AMZN', metric='capex', start='2025-01-01', end='2025-12-31') -> calc_bc1d79d6ffc0 = 131,819,000,000 (us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets, the GROSS purchase line).
4. calculate('subtract', <2>, <3>) -> 7,695,000,000, new calc_id (a flow minus a flow over the identical window; permitted).
5. (optional/trap) evaluate_formula(ticker='AMZN', name='free_cash_flow') -> calc_366dd8b8ab95 = -2,472,000,000, basis '2025-04-01..2026-03-31'.
6. respond(citations=[chunk_fef1f8cb72d9, chunk_2e3cfa95e763, <2>, <3>, <4>]).
The wrinkle that makes this a composition test: the named producer cannot be aimed at the period asked about. evaluate_formula's schema takes only `months` and `at` — no start/end — so it can NEVER return calendar-2025 FCF. The correct answer is reachable only by composing get_flow + get_flow + calculate by hand.
correct_answer_must: State Amazon's own figure: $11,194 million for the year ended 2025-12-31, from chunk_fef1f8cb72d9, with its own definition from chunk_2e3cfa95e763 — operating cash flow reduced by 'Purchases of property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales and incentives'. Any quotation marks must be verbatim (the V11-Q checker resolves them against the cited chunk). State the desk's number for the SAME window: $139,514M - $131,819M = $7,695 million over 2025-01-01..2025-12-31. Point out that the operating-cash-flow leg agrees EXACTLY ($139,514M in the filing and in financial_facts), so the whole gap sits on the capex leg. Name the reason and check it: the desk's capex is the gross purchase line while Amazon nets proceeds from sales and incentives — 131,819 - 128,320 = 3,499, exactly 11,194 - 7,695. NOT declare either figure wrong: free cash flow has no uniform definition, and SEC C&DI 102.07 — the authority the formula registry carries — says so outright. NOT answer with the trailing-twelve-month number: evaluate_formula(name='free_cash_flow') at the default months=12 lands on 2025-04-01..2026-03-31 and returns NEGATIVE $2,472M; a reply of roughly minus $2.5B against a question about +$11.2B is the sign-flipped failure this is built to catch. Name the period as the calendar year ended 2025-12-31, not 'last year' and not 'the last twelve months'.

q: msft net debt — and show me the actual lines you built it out of, i need to tie it back to the balance sheet
klass: SELF-KNOWLEDGE — justifying a number it produced, i.e. reading back its own derivation
failure_mode: NOTHING ON THE SURFACE READS THE CALC LEDGER BACK. evaluate_formula hands over a value, a calc_id and a definition STRING — never its input ids, never its component values — and no tool takes a calc_id and returns its derivation (trace_service is imported into definitions.py and registered as nothing). So 'show me the lines' is answerable only by RE-DERIVING with further calls. An agent that answers from the first call alone states component figures the cited calc_id does not hold and is refused with unverified_numbers, because numeric_verification._from_calc reads only the ledger row's own result — or it silently drops the itemisation and answers the label instead of the question. Exact inverse of self-surface-manifest: there the gate can see nothing, here the gate is the thing that bites.

All three legs re-verified live.

It returns NO input ids and NO component values — the dict is exactly {formula, ticker, value, calc_id, definition, basis, authority, note, unit_class}.

4. respond(citations=[calc_f60a79bc2cd7, fact_1f6cbb3811f2, the cash fact id, the current-portion and noncurrent fact ids]).
Three budgeted calls. MSFT is chosen deliberately over NVDA: NVDA also files debt_current_total and the containment.cover sibling-parent bug is STILL LIVE at HEAD (verified: evaluate_formula('NVDA','total_debt') = 34,366,000,000 = 33,366 + 1,000, double-counting the 1,000 current portion already inside long_term_debt_total). MSFT files no debt_current_total, so its cover is clean and the question tests composition rather than a known arithmetic defect.
correct_answer_must: Net debt = $8.157B as of 2026-03-31, stated WITH its definition (total debt less cash and equivalents), not as a bare label: 40,262 - 32,105 = 8,157, in millions. Total debt = $40.262B, and it must say this is a single reported line (us-gaap:LongTermDebt), NOT a sum: that line already contains both the $8.839B current portion and the $31.423B noncurrent piece, and 8,839 + 31,423 = 40,262 exactly. An answer that adds any of these together, or reports $31.423B as 'the debt', has failed. Cash = $32.105B, and it must be the unrestricted line (us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue), not cash_and_restricted_cash — restricted cash may not be netted against debt. Every component figure must carry its OWN fact_ id from get_balance_sheet; citing only the net_debt calc_id while stating 40.262 and 32.105 must fail the gate, and if it does not, the gate has a hole worth recording. All four figures are readings at ONE instant, 2026-03-31, and the answer must say so. It must NOT say Microsoft is net cash or that net debt is negative; at this date it is positive $8.157B. If it mentions commercial paper it must say MSFT did not report it at 2026-03-31 (last reported 2025-06-30) and that the figure was not carried forward. No verdict on whether that leverage is high.
